content:
If you just bought a new Mac, like the recently released Mac mini or Mac Studio, you might also want to pick up a new external display.

Below are my recommendations, covering multiple product categories, price points, and other factors.

Best Mac external displays

Apple Studio Display

When it comes to the best displays on the market, you can't not mention Apple's Studio Display. Although the price is on the high side, it features Apple's iconic design and comes with a 27-inch 5K display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 600 nits
  • Colour support: Wide colour gamut (P3), supporting 1 billion colours
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: 12-megapixel Center Stage camera, with Desk View support
  • True Tone technology: Automatically adjusts the display's colour temperature to match ambient lighting
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports (up to 120Gb/s) and two USB-C ports (up to 10Gb/s)
  • Host charging: Up to 96W

The Studio Display offers a range of configurations and different price points, which I've listed below. If you want a Mac experience close to that of an iMac, the Apple Studio Display is the obvious choice.

Standard glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Standard glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Apple Studio Display XDR

The Studio Display XDR was released earlier this year and offers several major advantages over the standard Studio Display, including mini-LED display technology and a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina XDR display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with mini-LED backlighting and 2,304 local dimming zones
  • Brightness: Up to 1,000 nits SDR brightness, 2,000 nits HDR peak brightness
  • Colour support: P3 and Adobe RGB wide colour gamut, supporting 1 billion colours
  • Refresh rate: 120Hz, with Adaptive Sync support
  • Host charging: Up to 140W

Of course, the price of these advantages is that it's even more expensive than the standard Studio Display.

Samsung M9 Smart Monitor

The 32-inch Samsung M9 Smart Monitor is an attractive option for Mac users because it features a 4K OLED panel. My colleague Justin Kahn over at 9to5Toys has already switched to this monitor and says it "has been really great paired with my Mac mini over the past few months."

  • Panel: 32-inch 4K OLED display (3840×2160 resolution), with anti-glare coating
  • Refresh rate: 165Hz
  • Ports: DisplayPort, HDMI, USB-C, 2 USB-A
  • Built-in camera: Yes, 4K
  • HDR support: Yes (HDR10/HDR10+)

Although it doesn't offer the 5K or 6K resolution of some other options on the list, you'll enjoy the benefits of OLED, including deeper blacks, better colour reproduction and contrast.

Buy the Samsung M9 OLED Smart Monitor:

LG UltraFine 6K

The LG UltraFine 6K is LG's evolution in the high-end display market. It features a 32-inch panel with a resolution of 6144 x 3456 pixels and a comprehensive range of ports. Here are the key specs:

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K Nano IPS Black display (6144×3456 resolution), 224 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Colour support: 98% DCI-P3 and 99.5% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colours (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • True Tone: None; supports auto-brightness adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports, one DisplayPort 2.1, one HDMI 2.1, two downstream USB-C ports and one upstream USB-C port
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt
  • Contrast ratio: 2,000:1

Here are the purchase links for the LG UltraFine 6K

Asus ProArt 5K Display

My colleague Jeff Benjamin tried this unit in person and I was immediately drawn to it. The Asus ProArt (PA27JCV) Display 5K offers the same 5K resolution (5120×2880) and the same 27-inch size, but at half the price of the Studio Display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 500 certified
  • Colour support: 99% DCI-P3, 100% sRGB and 95% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colours (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz, with Adaptive-Sync support
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient adjustment: Ambient light and backlight sensor automatically adjusts brightness and colour temperature
  • Ports: One USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode support, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C and a headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via USB-C

Watch Jeff's full review for all the details. If you're looking for a 5K display to pair with your Mac, the Asus ProArt is almost unbeatable.

Here are the purchase links for the Asus ProArt Display 5K:

Asus ProArt 6K Display

If you want a larger and higher-resolution option, Asus has you covered too. The new Asus ProArt Display 6K (PA32QCV) is a 32-inch display with a native resolution of 6016 x 3384. Jeff called it "absurdly good value" in his review.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K IPS display (6016×3384 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits, HDR peak 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Colour support: 98% DCI-P3 and 100% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colours (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz, with Adaptive-Sync support (48–60Hz)
  • Webcam: None
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, USB-C and USB-A hub connections, and a headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt 4

The biggest selling point of the ASUS ProArt 6K Display may be its price. It's considerably cheaper than some of the most popular 4K and 5K displays on the market.

Here are the purchase links for the ASUS ProArt 6K display:

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K (S80HF)

Samsung's ViewFinity S8 5K is another attractive option to pair with your new Mac, offering 5K resolution.

  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits
  • Colour support: 99% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colours; HDR10
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient adjustment: Adaptive Picture automatically adjusts brightness based on ambient light
  • Ports: One USB-C port with 90W power delivery, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-A ports, one downstream USB-C port, Ethernet and a headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via USB-C

Here are the purchase links for the Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K:

BenQ 27-inch 5K PD2730S Thunderbolt Display

This might be my current favourite on the list. The BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K display comes with a range of Mac-friendly features, the most prominent of which is of course the crisp, sharp 5K resolution.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with Nano Matte coating
  • Brightness: Typical and peak 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 400 certified
  • Colour support: 100% sRGB, 100% Rec.709 and 98% P3, supporting 1.07 billion colours
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • Ports: One upstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one downstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one upstream USB-C port, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4 and a headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Hotkey Puck G3: Physical external controller with custom function support

Here are the purchase links for the BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K display:

Read our full review: BenQ's 27-inch 5K Thunderbolt 4 designer display is a true contender to the Apple Studio Display

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Display

If you want a 32-inch display to pair with your new Mac but want to stay under $1,000, this is one of the most attractive options. However, the biggest downside is that you only "get" 4K resolution instead of 5K. That said, it comes with a wide range of port options, and the 32-inch panel is priced under $1,000.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black display (3840×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch
  • Colour support: 98% P3, 100% sRGB and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colours
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient adjustment: No automatic ambient light colour temperature adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 3 ports, two HDMI 2.0 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, USB-B and a headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 85W via Thunderbolt 3

Here are the purchase links for the BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt display:

Read our full review: Should 32-inch 4K Mac displays have been vetoed from the start?

Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultra-Wide

If you want to pair your Mac with an ultra-wide display, the Dell U4025QW is one of the best options on the market. It packs 5K resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate into a 40-inch display. There are also plenty of ports, a matte screen finish and more.

  • Display: 39.7-inch curved 5K2K IPS Black display (5120×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch, 21:9 aspect ratio, 2500R curvature
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits, HDR peak 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Colour support: 99% DCI-P3, 99% Display P3, 100% sRGB and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colours
  • Refresh rate: Up to 120Hz, with VRR support
  • Webcam: None
  • Ambient adjustment: Ambient light sensor automatically adjusts brightness and colour temperature
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-C ports, five USB-A ports, 2.5Gb Ethernet and audio output
  • Host charging: Up to 140W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Speakers: Two 9W speakers

Here are the purchase links for the Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultra-Wide display:

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC

Looking to enter the ultra-wide display market at a more affordable price, the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC is an option, currently available at nearly half price. While it lacks all the bells and whistles of other options, you still get a 34-inch ultra-wide curved display with plenty of ports, including a Thunderbolt 4 port with power delivery support.

  • Display: 34-inch ultra-wide curved display, Ultra-WQHD resolution (3440×1440), 1000R curvature for an immersive viewing experience.
  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits.
  • Webcam: None.
  • Ports: One Thunderbolt 4 port (providing up to 90W power delivery), one HDMI 2.0 port, one DisplayPort 1.2, three USB-A 3.0 ports, one RJ45 Ethernet port and one 3.5mm headphone jack.

Here are the purchase links for the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC:

Summary

These are just some of the best external display options to pair with your new Mac. They all offer excellent macOS integration, rich connectivity options, and unique sizes and form factors.

Have you recently bought a new Mac? Which display are you pairing it with? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
